notes: Each eval runs with the skill and without it (baseline). A separate grader sees only the output and the assertions. 'common_assertions' apply to every eval unless skip_common is true. kind=format checks the skill's output shape (baselines are expected to miss these); kind=substance checks correctness and safety.

common_assertions.check: The output is a complete plan. It does not stop at interview questions or ask the user to answer before giving the plan.
Has an Assumptions → Decisions table; every row says whether the assumption was stated by the user or inferred.
Ends by offering 2–3 alternative architectures to compare.

Every number (percentages, prices, week counts, thresholds, market shares) either comes from the user's prompt, is cited to a source, or is explicitly labelled as a suggested starting value, estimate, or heuristic. Unlabelled invented figures fail.

Does not state that a named vendor signs a BAA, is HIPAA-eligible, SOC 2 attested, or PCI compliant without citing that vendor's documentation, and never claims a 'HIPAA certification'. Generic advice ('confirm a BAA with each vendor') passes. N/A if no such claims are needed.
No two statements in the output contradict each other (e.g., 'data not stored' vs a retention period; a platform placed in two different tiers; an assumption that doesn't match the plan's numbers).

Each platform appears in exactly one tier. Anything built in parallel with Tier 1 is presented as a Tier 1 launch track. Every Tier 2+ tier starts after the previous tier ships plus a measurement window, and its metric gate can actually be measured inside that window.
Tier 1 release gates contain no retention or engagement targets (those only gate later tiers).

Tools, services, and store names match their platform (e.g., no SwiftLint/TestFlight/watchOS in an Android plan; no Play Console in an iOS plan) and nothing is carried over from an unrelated scenario.
Store policies, API levels, and AI model names are current as of the run date, cited, or explicitly flagged as needing verification. No outdated model names presented as current.

If the prompt does not state team size: assumes a solo developer working part-time, labels it Inferred, and scales timelines UP accordingly (in the actual week numbers). Never assumes a larger team and never scales down. N/A if the prompt states team size.

evals.prompt: I want to build a CRM for small real-estate teams. Agents manage leads, brokers see pipeline reports. What platforms should I build first? Answers to your usual questions: 2 full-time engineers (TypeScript/web); per-seat monthly subscription; agents need phone access in the field but always-online is fine; SMB brokerages first, SOC 2 expected in year 2; US only. Don't ask further questions.
evals.expected_output: Web-First plan using the stated answers (2 full-time engineers, so no solo scaling). SOC 2 on the roadmap with audit logging from day 1; SOC 2 described as an independent CPA audit. Metric gate for Tier 2 measurable within the window.

assertions.check: Recommends the Web-First template.
Uses the answers supplied in the prompt (2 full-time engineers, per-seat subscription, US-only, SOC 2 in year 2) rather than overriding them with defaults.
Treats SOC 2 as an independent CPA audit/attestation, not a legal or counsel sign-off.

evals.prompt: Fitness tracking app for gym-goers in India, I'm a solo Kotlin developer. Design the architecture. Don't ask questions; infer anything missing.
evals.expected_output: Android-First, native Kotlin. Solo developer stated; hours not stated, so part-time default (~3x) or an explicitly flagged full-time assumption, applied to the week numbers. API 36+ and minSdk 24 with a source. Android-native tooling throughout. India's DPDP Act flagged.

assertions.check: Recommends the Android-First template.
Scales the timeline for a solo developer, states the multiplier, and the plan's week numbers actually reflect it. Full-time must be labelled as an inference, not as stated.
Uses target API 36+ and minSdk 24 (not API 34 or minSdk 21) and cites or links the source.
Uses Android-native tooling and services (e.g., detekt/ktlint, Play Console testing tracks, Health Connect, Wear OS) with no iOS-only items in the Android plan.
Flags India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act (or local privacy law for India) as a compliance item.

evals.prompt: I want to build a Chrome extension that summarizes articles with an LLM. Which platforms and architecture? Don't ask questions; infer anything missing.
evals.expected_output: Browser-Extension-First with Manifest V3. Inference placement compared, including built-in on-device browser AI. Per-user inference cost tied to pricing. No cross-user caches, consistent privacy statements, no model versions from memory, Safari packaging cost noted.

assertions.check: Recommends Browser-Extension-First (not Web-First).
Compares cloud vs on-device inference, and considers built-in browser/OS AI APIs as an on-device option.
Connects per-user inference cost to the pricing or free-tier limits.
Plans for Manifest V3.
Any cache of article content or summaries is keyed per user (or the output avoids shared caching of user-supplied/paywalled content). N/A if no cache is proposed.
Notes that Safari extensions need an Xcode app wrapper / Apple Developer Program / App Store distribution, or explicitly defers Safari.

evals.prompt: Telehealth app where patients message their therapist and log mood daily. Should I go iOS first or web first? Don't ask questions; infer anything missing.
evals.expected_output: Flags PHI and applies the Compliance Overlay without naming unverified BAA vendors. Addresses the business-associate relationship with therapists. Crisis-protocol Tier 1 gate. Deletion vs record retention reconciled. Counsel confirmation.

assertions.check: Flags regulated health data (PHI/HIPAA).
Addresses that the company is likely a business associate of the therapists/practices and signs BAAs with them.
Requires BAAs from every vendor touching PHI without asserting specific vendors are BAA-eligible (unless cited).
Includes a Tier 1 crisis-handling gate (e.g., 988 or local crisis line routing, 'not for emergencies' notice, escalation policy).
Reconciles user deletion requests with medical-record retention obligations instead of promising unconditional purge.
Tells the user to confirm the compliance approach with counsel.

evals.prompt: Two of us want to ship a habit tracker on iPhone and Android at the same time within 3 months. We both know React. Native or cross-platform? Don't ask questions; infer anything missing.
evals.expected_output: Cross-platform (React Native/Expo) with Mobile-First sequencing, explained by team + skills + timeline. Monetization in Tier 1. No unsourced code-share %. No false Flutter claims.

assertions.check: Recommends a cross-platform implementation (React Native/Expo) and explains why from team size, React skills, and timeline.
Uses Mobile-First (or a named platform-first template) for tier sequencing.
Includes monetization/paywall in Tier 1.
Makes no false capability claims about Flutter, React Native, or native frameworks (e.g., 'Flutter has no HealthKit support').

evals.prompt: We make a BLE smart ring. Need a companion app that syncs sleep data to the cloud and a dashboard for users. Architecture? Don't ask questions; infer anything missing.
evals.expected_output: Hardware-companion path named explicitly; background BLE and firmware OTA flow; BLE reliability/battery Tier 1 gates; FTC Health Breach Notification Rule for consumer sleep data; solo part-time default.

assertions.check: Uses and names the hardware-companion combination (e.g., Mobile-First companion + Web dashboard).
Covers background BLE sync limits on iOS and Android and a firmware OTA update flow with rollback.
Tier 1 gates include BLE reliability and battery impact.
Flags the FTC Health Breach Notification Rule (consumer health data not covered by HIPAA), including notifying the FTC.

evals.prompt: Design the architecture for a marketplace where home cooks sell meals: buyers order on their phones, cooks manage menus and orders on a laptop. Run without asking me questions.
evals.expected_output: No questions. Mobile-First (buyers) + Web-First (cooks) on one backend. PCI via hosted payments with SAQ A. Cottage food laws as a launch blocker. Solo part-time default.

assertions.check: Asks no questions.
Combines Mobile-First (buyers) and Web-First (cooks) on one shared backend and names the combination.
Uses hosted payment fields and names SAQ A correctly (no invented certifications).
Flags state cottage food laws (or equivalent local food-sale rules) as a launch blocker.

evals.prompt: I'm building a multiplayer mobile game with Unity. What platforms should I launch on? Don't ask questions; infer anything missing.
evals.expected_output: States games are outside the skill's templates, explains why, gives only general platform-order guidance and engine/store resources; no filled-in plan.

assertions.check: States that games are outside this skill's templates.
Does not produce a filled-in template plan.
Gives general platform-order guidance and points to engine/store resources.
Any documentation URLs look like real official URLs (e.g., docs.unity3d.com). Flag any that look invented; a human should click them.
